answer: An agent marketplace uses a bonding contract as the bridge from a new identity to paid work: every account, a vertex in its trading graph, must lock $100 for 30 days before bidding on tasks such as drawing a quill. Creating 1,000 sybils therefore ties up $100,000 for a month; splitting one balance among names cannot unlock extra accounts. This does not eliminate sybils, but makes each additional identity costly.
